page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-64 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4d family. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs and 248.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators.

Operating on a dedicated CPU allocation, the instance provides predictable compute resources. The absence of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated vCPUs relative to memory makes it a structured option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe drives.

This server is designed for workloads requiring substantial parallel processing capabilities. Suitable applications include high-performance web serving, batch processing, continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, and distributed compute tasks that scale efficiently across 64 dedicated cores.
